Sending your dog away for 4 weeks is a HUGE decision, and I was definitely nervous going into the Board and Train program. You’re trusting someone with a member of your family, so I had a million questions and wanted to make sure I was making the right choice. Looking back now, choosing The Canine Club was one of the best decisions I could have made.

The difference from before the program to now is honestly night and day. I didn’t just get my dog back knowing a few commands. I got back a dog who actually understands structure, boundaries, communication, and what is expected of them. Walks are more enjoyable, everyday life is less stressful, and I feel so much more confident handling different situations because Raza didn’t only train my dog, he taught ME how to continue everything at home.

That was probably my favorite part of the entire experience. Raza genuinely cares about the relationship between the dog and the owner. He takes the time to explain the why behind everything instead of just telling you what to do. You can immediately tell how passionate and knowledgeable he is about dogs, and that same energy carries over to his team.

The communication throughout the 4 weeks was amazing too. Getting updates and being able to see the progress happening made being away from my dog so much easier. Every week I could see more confidence, better obedience, and more control developing.

The go home lesson was incredibly thorough and made me realize how much work actually goes into this program. They didn’t just hand me my dog and send me on my way. Raza made sure I understood the training, the equipment, the commands, and how to maintain the results long term.

A 4 week Board and Train is definitely an investment, but after experiencing the results firsthand, I completely understand why. The amount of time, consistency, knowledge, and individual attention that goes into each dog is worth it.

If you’re frustrated, overwhelmed, or feel like you’ve tried everything with your dog, give The Canine Club a chance. I wish I would have done it sooner.

Thank you Raza and the entire Canine Club team for taking such amazing care of my dog and giving us a completely different quality of life together. You guys are truly incredible at what you do. ❤️🐾

10/10 experience and I would recommend The Canine Club of Chicago without hesitation.

The Canine Club of Chicago and their 4 week Board and Train program. Sending our Labrador Retriever, Goose, here was one of the best decisions we have ever made for him and for our family.

Before training, everyday life with Goose could honestly be exhausting. He is a loving, amazing dog, but he had so much energy and very little impulse control. Walks were a struggle because of pulling and getting overly excited by everything around him. He would have a hard time settling down, listening when distracted, holding commands, and understanding when it was time to be calm. We found ourselves constantly repeating commands, correcting the same behaviors, and feeling like Goose was running the household instead of us being able to simply enjoy him.

The difference after four weeks is incredible.

Goose came home still having the same happy, goofy personality we love, but now he has structure, confidence, patience, and an understanding of what is expected of him. His leash walking has completely changed. Instead of being dragged around or constantly fighting for his attention, we can actually enjoy peaceful walks together. His obedience around distractions is on another level. His place command has been life changing in the house, especially when guests come over, food is being prepared, or we simply need him to relax. His recall, sit, down, stay, overall engagement, and ability to settle have improved tremendously.

What impressed us most is that this was not about turning Goose into a robot. He is still Goose. He is still playful, affectionate, excited, and full of personality. He just finally understands how to control himself and communicate with us.

Raza’s passion for dogs and training is obvious from the moment you speak with him. He genuinely cares about the dogs in his program and takes pride in producing real results, not just teaching a few tricks for a video. He took the time to understand Goose as an individual dog and worked through the behaviors that were actually making our daily life difficult.

The communication throughout the program was another huge reason we had such a great experience. We felt comfortable knowing how Goose was doing and could see the progress being made. The team was professional, knowledgeable, patient, and clearly invested in his success.

The go home experience was also extremely valuable because they did not just hand us a trained dog and send us on our way. They showed us how to communicate with Goose, how to maintain his training, and how to continue building on everything he learned. That part made us feel confident that the results would actually carry over into our everyday life.

A Board and Train program is definitely an investment, and we thought seriously about it before enrolling Goose. After seeing the results, I can genuinely say it was worth every penny. The quality of life improvement alone has been priceless. We are able to take Goose more places, enjoy walks, have people over, relax at home, and include him in our lives without constantly worrying about what behavior we are going to have to manage next.

The biggest change is that we are finally able to enjoy our dog instead of constantly struggling with our dog.

If you are considering The Canine Club of Chicago and wondering whether the 4 week Board and Train is worth it, our experience with Goose is an absolute yes. The results exceeded our expectations, the communication was excellent, and you can tell Raza and his team truly care about what they do.

Thank you to Raza and everyone at The Canine Club of Chicago for giving us an even better version of the dog we already loved. The difference this program has made in our home and in our relationship with Goose has honestly been life changing.

Unfortunately really disappointed. This was our experience:

I spent months trying to manage my dog’s aggression on my own before finally reaching out to The Canine Club of Chicago. I talked to several trainers around the city, but after speaking with Raza, it was obvious he approached dog training differently. He wasn’t trying to make unrealistic promises or sell me on magic fixes. He took the time to explain why my dog was behaving the way he was, what the training process would look like, and what would be expected from me after the program.

I enrolled my dog in the aggression board and train program, and it ended up being one of the best investments I’ve ever made.

From day one, communication was outstanding. Raza and his team kept me updated with videos, photos, and detailed explanations of what they were working on and why. It never felt like I had dropped my dog off and was left wondering what was happening. Watching the progress week after week gave me so much confidence that my dog was in the right hands.

The biggest difference was that they didn’t just teach obedience commands. They focused on changing my dog’s mindset, building confidence, creating structure, and teaching clear communication. By the time my dog came home, the transformation was incredible. Walks became enjoyable instead of stressful. I wasn’t constantly scanning for other dogs or worrying about every person we passed. My dog was calm, attentive, and actually looked to me for direction instead of reacting to everything around us.

The go home lesson was just as valuable as the training itself. Raza spent as much time teaching me as he did training my dog. He made sure I understood how to maintain everything at home and answered every question without making me feel rushed. It’s obvious that he genuinely wants every dog to succeed long after they leave the program.

What impressed me most was how much Raza genuinely cares. He treats every dog as an individual instead of using the same approach for every case. You can tell this isn’t just a job for him. He’s passionate about helping dogs and helping owners build better relationships with them.

If you’re looking for dog training in Chicago, especially if you’re dealing with aggression or reactivity, I cannot recommend The Canine Club of Chicago enough. Raza and his team are professional, knowledgeable, honest, and truly dedicated to getting real results. They didn’t just improve my dog’s behavior. They completely changed the way we live together, and I honestly wish I had found them sooner.

The transformation was incredible. Before training, walks were stressful, commands were optional, and I constantly had to manage unwanted behaviors. After graduating from The Canine Club, my dog walks politely on a leash, responds the first time I give a command, has dramatically better impulse control, and is much calmer and more confident in new environments. When it was time to come home, Raza spent plenty of time making sure I understood everything. He explained why the training works, how to maintain it, and answered every question without ever making me feel rushed. It’s obvious that he genuinely wants every dog and owner to succeed long after the program ends.

The entire team is professional, knowledgeable, and truly passionate about what they do. You can tell they care about every dog that walks through their doors. Their communication, attention to detail, and commitment to producing reliable results are second to none.

Investing in this board and train program was one of the best decisions I’ve ever made for my dog. It has made everyday life so much more enjoyable and strengthened the bond between us. We sent Basso to The Canine Club Bootcamp. We now use Raza for home boarding when we’re away where he can continue reinforcing Basso’s training. And best of all, Basso is beside-himself excited every time we drop him off with Raza so we know he’s happy when we’re away (plus Raza sends video updates so we don’t miss him quite as much).

I hired Raza for puppy training in November 2024 and opted for the $800 package with 10 sessions. Why a 2-star review? Because Raza knows dogs, but he DOES NOT know business. For multiple training sessions and pick-up and drop-off appointments for boarding, he was significantly late or asking to change days/times at the last minute. He always has dog-ate-my-homework excuses: he and his girlfriend had a fight and she threw his phone across the room breaking it; he hit a deer and his car is totaled; his brother lost his house keys and he had to go home to let him in; he ran into traffic because of the weather; he left his phone at a restaurant and someone stole it; he got pulled over by the police, on and on, you get the picture. On average he’s 10-15 minutes late, at worst he’s been 30 minutes-1 hour late. On 3 separate occasions he offered to compensate me with an additional session. He refused to refund me unused sessions, so I was stuck. Frankly, he doesn’t have the discipline to have a rigid business policy like that. We had a come-to-Jesus conversation about his behavior in which he promised the flakiness would stop. The final straw for me was him being unresponsive on the day of  pick-up for boarding on February 11, 2025, the night before an early morning flight (which he knew). We agreed in writing and in-person on the day/time a week in advance. The day before, I get no confirmation. The day of, I messaged him throughout the day looking for confirmation with no response. I had to scramble at the last minute to find another boarding option that evening. An hour AFTER the agreed upon pick-up time, he messages me from an email address with another lame excuse, claiming he could pick up my puppy in an hour (which would be 2+ hours after the agreed upon time of 7pm). At this point, I’ve already taken my dog to another business for boarding. Fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice, shame on me. I will no longer be using his services and cannot confidently recommend him. My puppy did make progress with play biting, potty training, crate training, and “sit” and “place” commands. However, any decent trainer could have accomplished that AND been respectful of my time, and a puppy’s need for consistent complete sessions. I hope he finds a way to become a more responsible and polished business owner. Don’t treat this like a side hustle, and don’t think I’m your homie and your excuses are gonna slide. I am an Afrolatina woman, so I am not stereotyping him when I say: Do better.
